title: Electrostatics as a Stress Theory in $\mathbb R^3$ : Free and Bound Charge, Gauge Invariance, and Mechanical Interactions
summary: We formulate electrostatics in \rthree as the simplest instance of the theory of stresses: the virtual velocity field of continuum mechanics is simply replaced by a scalar potential field. A charge distribution is then a linear functional on potential fields whose value is the potential energy, and it is represented by a volume charge density and by surface charge densities on the boundaries of subbodies. Cauchy's theorem gives a vector field $\boldsymbol P$, the analog of the traction stress, and a scalar field $r$, so that the energy is $\int(r\varphi+\boldsymbol P\cdot\nabla\varphi)dV$.…
